messages.author: 3ddef94288961813
messages.subject: /RApacheInfo - gives Internal Server Error
parts:
Hi,

I am using OpenSuse 11.4 with Apache httpd 2.2.22 built with APR 1.4.6 and APR-util 1.4.1, and rapache 1.1.21, R2.15.0
I created a skeleton httpd.conf file with the following:

Port 80
LogLevel debug
DefaultType text/plain
LoadModule  R_module  /usr/local/apache2/modules/mod_R.so
<Location /RApacheInfo>
    SetHandler  r-info
</Location>

There are no other modules except for what's builtin. When I try to access http://localhost/RApacheInfo, I get the following error in the apache  log file:

[Sun Jun 24 05:23:23 2012] [warn] pid file /www/apache2/p8123/logs/httpd.pid overwritten -- Unclean shutdown of previous Apache run?
[Sun Jun 24 05:23:23 2012] [notice] Apache/2.2.22 (Unix) mod_R/1.1.21 R/2.15.0 configured -- resuming normal operations
[Sun Jun 24 05:23:23 2012] [info] Server built: Jun 21 2012 23:40:09
[Sun Jun 24 05:23:23 2012] [debug] prefork.c(1023): AcceptMutex: sysvsem (default: sysvsem)
[Sun Jun 24 05:23:46 2012] [error] [client ::1] File does not exist: /www/htdocs/favicon.ico
[Sun Jun 24 05:24:01 2012] [error] [client ::1] rApache Notice!
Error in gzfile(file, mode) : cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In is.na(st) :
  is.na() applied to non-(list or vector) of type 'closure'
2: In gzfile(file, mode) :
  cannot open compressed file '/tmp/libloc_109_7a453f33328e97b4.rds', probable reason 'Permission denied'
[Sun Jun 24 05:24:01 2012] [error] [client ::1] File does not exist: /www/htdocs/favicon.ico


But if I add another directive to my httpd.conf file such as:
<Directory /www/htdocs/R>
    SetHandler  r-script
    RHandler    sys.source
</Directory>
And create a file such as test1.r, test2.r, etc. then http://localhost/R/<filename> calls the  appropriate script and produces the run output.

This is all very confounding!! I will greatly appreciate someone could please point out what am I doing wrong and what's the best fix.

Regards
Dinesh

messages.author: 3ddef94288961813
messages.subject: Re: /RApacheInfo - gives Internal Server Error
parts:
Hi Jeff,

A great hunch!!! 

To test /tmp access condition, I created a small test file - test2.r:
sink(file="/tmp/written-by-rapache", append=T, split=T);
cat(sprintf("date time is %s\n", Sys.time()));
sink(NULL);
and accessed it as http://localhost/R/test2.r. This page loads fine. The output file is there in /tmp and getting appended correctly on every page refresh. 
The /tmp looks very ordinary, as below:
/tmp 18:30:58 886> ls -ld /tmp  /tmp/written-by-rapache /tmp/libloc_109_7a453f33328e97b4.rds 
drwxrwxrwt 175 root   root   12288 Jun 24 18:29 /tmp
-rw-r--r--   1 daemon daemon  1944 Jun 21 23:51 /tmp/libloc_109_7a453f33328e97b4.rds
-rw-r--r--   1 dinesh users    198 Jun 24 18:27 /tmp/written-by-rapache
where the libloc....rds file is the one showing open trouble in the apache error log. But you would notice the owners of the two tmp files are so different, and that is because I changed my test apache user/group over the last few days. All I had to do was blow away the old rds file and there, puft!

I imagine this can easily recur since this rds file name does not appear to depend on - port number, user name, group name. On a multi-owner machine I may not even have control over it. Will appreciate if you could shed some light on this.

Thanks and regards
Dinesh
